intake.question: How long has this been going on?

options.label: On and off for over a year

intake.question: What do you want from it?

plan.title: What you have plenty of, and what you lack

strong.text:
Your chart is the strong kind, {dm_short}, and that adds a twist to why you stay. Strong charts don't usually stay out of fear. They stay because they assume they're in charge of it. You can leave whenever you want, so there's no rush, so you don't. Meanwhile months go by. Ask yourself a blunt question: if you're the one in control, why hasn't anything been decided? Sometimes the answer is that you like the option more than the person. Sometimes it's that you're waiting for them to step up so you don't have to ask. Either way, being able to leave at any moment is not the same as choosing to stay. Make it a choice.

A practical way to make it a choice: give the current setup a review date, the way you'd review anything else you've invested in. Put it in your calendar a month from now. On that day, answer three questions on paper. Am I getting what I want? Have I asked for it? Did anything change after I asked? If all three answers are no, the review is over and so is the arrangement.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can leave any time, so you never do. Cute. Pick on purpose.

weak.text:
Your chart is the weak kind, {dm_short}, and that colors why you stay. A weak chart tends to treat any warmth as something it should be grateful for. A good night, a sweet text, an invite out of nowhere, and you feel lucky, so you don't ask for more in case asking breaks it. That makes an undefined thing feel safer than it is. Here's a test. Imagine a friend describing your exact setup to you, with the same texts, the same gaps, the same weekends. Would you tell them they're lucky, or would you tell them they deserve to know where they stand? Give yourself the same advice you'd give them.

It also helps to notice the moments when you feel most grateful to them. Gratitude is lovely, but in an undefined relationship it can work like a sedative. You feel lucky after a good night, so you stop asking questions for another two weeks. Next time you feel that rush, enjoy it, and then ask yourself one quiet question the morning after: was that a good night, or a good relationship?

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: What would you tell a friend in your exact spot? Say that to yourself.

strong.text:
A note for strong charts: you usually do know what you want. The hesitation isn't confusion, it's pride. Saying it first feels like giving away the advantage. But a situationship has no advantage to keep. Whoever names the thing first doesn't lose. They just get information sooner. You're good at decisions. This is one, so treat it that way: write the want, set a date to say it, and keep the date like you'd keep any other commitment.

One caution while you write it: strong charts sometimes describe what they want as a list of what the other person should do. Turn each line around so it describes the relationship instead. Not "they need to text more," but "I want to hear from you most days." The second version is something two people can agree to. The first is a performance review.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Saying it first isn't losing. It's just finding out sooner.

weak.text:
A note for weak charts: the want is often there, buried under what you think you're allowed to want. You might shrink it in advance, asking for a little so it feels safe to ask at all. Try writing the full version first, the one you'd say if you knew the answer would be yes. Then compare it to the small version you were going to ask for. The gap between them is what you've been settling for. You don't have to demand the big one. Just stop pretending it doesn't exist.

Then pick one line from the big version and say it out loud, to yourself, in a normal voice. Not apologetically. Weak charts often discover that the want sounds much more reasonable spoken than it felt in their head. Wanting to be someone's person, wanting a plan for the weekend, wanting to be introduced to their friends: none of it is excessive. It is the ordinary furniture of a relationship.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write the version you'd ask for if you knew they'd say yes. Look at it.

strong.text:
Strong charts read signals with confidence, and sometimes that's the problem. You decide what a late reply means, then treat your reading as fact. You may also send signals you don't notice, like going cool to see whether they chase. That's a test, not a message, and tests make everything blurrier. Try reporting instead of signaling for two weeks. If you're busy, say so. If you liked the date, say so. If something bothered you, say that too, briefly. Clear input usually gets clearer output.

And when you do read a signal, check it once before acting on it. A simple "You went quiet this week, everything okay?" costs nothing and replaces a theory with a fact. Strong charts tend to skip that step because they trust their read. Your read is good. It's just better with one data point from the other person.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Going cold to see if they chase is a test, not a signal. Report instead.

weak.text:
Weak charts read signals anxiously, and every gap becomes a verdict. A slow reply means you did something wrong. A warm night means everything is fine. You ride each signal up and down, and that ride is tiring. Try collecting instead of reacting. For two weeks, write down what actually happens: who texted, who planned, who canceled. Don't interpret, just record. At the end, the list tells you more than any single message, and it tells you without you having to guess at midnight.

When the anxiety spikes anyway, put a timer on it. Give yourself ten minutes to worry properly, write the worst-case story down, then close the note and do something with your hands. Worry that gets a container gets smaller. Worry that gets the whole evening grows into a theory you'll half believe by morning.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Don't decode every text. Keep a plain list for two weeks. The list knows.

strong.text:
Strong-chart warning for the talk: don't run it like a negotiation. You'll be tempted to open with terms, deadlines or a summary of everything that's been unclear. It can land like an ultimatum even when you mean it as honesty. Start with what you feel and what you want, then ask a real question and wait through the silence. If their answer isn't what you hoped, resist the urge to argue them into a better one. A yes you had to win isn't the kind that lasts.

Choose the setting with the same care you'd choose an argument you wanted to win, and then do the opposite of winning. Side by side works better than face to face: a walk, a drive, cooking together. It lowers the stakes. And keep your phone away. If they need a few days to answer, agree on a day to pick it up again, and then really do pick it up on that day.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: If you have to argue them into a yes, it's not a yes.

weak.text:
Weak-chart warning for the talk: don't soften it until it says nothing. You might start with I know you're busy, and it's totally fine if not, and by the end you've answered the question for them. Say the want in one sentence, without the cushions. Then stop talking. If their answer is vague, you're allowed to ask again: what does that mean for us? Being clear doesn't make you difficult. It makes you someone they can actually answer.

It helps to rehearse once, out loud, with a friend or alone. Not to script every line, just to hear yourself say the main sentence without shrinking it. If your voice wobbles, that's fine. Wobbly and clear still counts as clear. And plan something kind for yourself afterward, whatever the answer is. A meal with a friend, a film, an early night.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Say it in one sentence. No cushions. Then let the quiet sit there.

strong.text:
For a strong chart, the line is rarely the problem. Holding it kindly is. When you decide something's over, you can switch off fast and leave the other person wondering what happened. So add one rule to your line: when you go, you say so. A short, clear message, not a disappearance and not a lecture. Strength that ends things cleanly earns respect, even from people who wanted a different ending.

Also check that your line isn't secretly a test. Strong charts sometimes set a boundary and then wait to see if the other person will cross it, half hoping they do so the decision is made for them. That's leaving with extra steps. If you already know you want out, you don't need them to fail a test first. You can simply decide.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: When you leave, say so. Clean and kind. No vanishing act.

weak.text:
For a weak chart, the line tends to move. You set it, they step over it, you redraw it a little further back and call that understanding. Write your line down, and add what you'll do if it's crossed. Not a threat, a plan. If they cancel last minute three times, I stop making plans first. A line with a plan is much easier to keep than a line made of hope.

Tell one friend your line, too. Not to police you, just so it exists somewhere outside your head. Lines that only live inside a weak chart tend to get renegotiated at night. A friend who can say "you told me three cancellations, this is four" is the kindest kind of accountability, and it saves you from having to argue with yourself.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A boundary with no plan is just a wish. Write what you'll do.

strong.text:
Strong charts tend to land on their feet, so the risk afterward isn't collapse. It's skipping the lesson. You'll be busy and social and fine within a week. Before you move on, write down one thing you'll do differently next time from the very start. Ask earlier, say it sooner, notice the drift sooner. That one note is what turns a situationship into experience instead of a rerun.

If it turns into something real, bring the same honesty in early. Strong charts sometimes relax once they've won the label and stop saying what they need. Keep the habit of the talk. A five-minute check-in every few weeks, "how are we doing," keeps you from sliding into a new kind of vagueness with a better name.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fine in a week, sure. Write one lesson first or you'll rerun this.

weak.text:
Weak charts often take the ending harder than the situation seemed to justify, because so much hope went into it. That's not silly. Give yourself a few soft weeks: friends, sleep, things that ask nothing of you. And keep the main lesson small and kind: next time, I'll ask what this is sooner, because I deserve to know. That's all. You don't need to become a different person. You just need to ask one question earlier.

If it does become something real, keep a bit of the independence you built while things were unclear. Your friends, your plans, your evenings that belong to you. A relationship is healthier when both people arrive with full lives. Proving you're in doesn't require giving up your whole world. Being chosen doesn't mean disappearing into it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Next time, ask what it is sooner. That's the whole lesson. Be gentle.

peer_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {dm_el}, your own element. Saju calls this the peer family: friends, rivals, reflections of you. Lots of it makes you independent and slightly competitive, even in romance. In an undefined thing, that tends to become a standoff. Nobody volunteers to care more, and you are very good at not caring more, at least on the outside. The upside is that you don't need this to work out to be okay. The downside is that two people protecting their independence can drift for a year. Someone has to go first. It might as well be the one who can handle either answer.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A chart full of you. So who cares more? Neither of you, loudly. For a year.

output_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. That's the output family: charm, wit, expression, the flirty text at the right moment. With a strong Day Master behind it, you're fun to be undefined with, and you know it. Output also loves freedom and dislikes rules, so labels can feel like a cage you'd rather joke about than discuss. Watch for the pattern where you perform the connection instead of having it, the great banter, the inside jokes, and no sentence that says what you want. Your words are your gift. Use one of them for the real thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Great banter. Zero clarity. Use one of those clever sentences for the real thing.

wealth_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. That's the wealth family: what you pursue and manage. A strong chart handles it well, so you're often the one who plans, books, decides where to eat. Undefined, that easily becomes you running the whole thing while they enjoy the ride. It also means you may treat the relationship as something to win or secure. Ask yourself whether you want this person or whether you want to close the deal. They feel similar from inside. They lead to very different conversations.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A person isn't a contract. Check which one you're chasing.

power_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}. That's the power family: rules, standards, respectability. A strong chart can carry it, so you have a clear sense of what a proper relationship looks like, and a situationship probably bothers you more than you admit. You might be holding back because defining it feels like admitting you've been in something improper. It isn't improper. It's just unfinished. Your standards are useful here. Name them out loud, and let them decide for you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your standards are already written. Read them aloud. They'll decide for you.

resource_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. That's the resource family: comfort, thought, security. You're well cushioned, which makes it easy to think about this situationship endlessly without moving it. You've probably analyzed their attachment style, your attachment style and the attachment style of their dog. All that thinking feels productive. It mostly isn't. Pick one action this week, any action. Ask them to a specific plan, or ask the question. Thought is your comfort zone. A tiny bit of action will tell you more.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You've analyzed this from every angle. Time for one small action instead.

output_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. That's the output family: giving, expressing, performing. On a weak chart it drains you. In this setup you might be doing all the entertaining, the funny texts, the thoughtful gifts, the effort to stay interesting, while getting less back. It can feel like auditioning for a part that hasn't been cast. Notice how tired you are after you see them. Good connections leave you a bit fuller. If this one leaves you emptier, that's real information, and it has nothing to do with how hard you try.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're auditioning every week. For a role they never actually cast.

wealth_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. That's the wealth family: wanting, reaching, holding. Classical readers call this setup wealth heavy and self light, too much to hold with too little behind you. Here, you could be carrying the whole thing: keeping plans alive, keeping the mood good, keeping it going. That's a lot of holding for someone who isn't being held back. Let go of one task this week. Don't plan the next date. See who reaches. It's not a game. It's a way to find out whether the weight is shared.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Don't plan the next one. Just see who reaches. Not a game, just information.

power_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}. That's the power family: pressure, expectations, being judged. On a weak chart it makes you careful. You may be on your best behavior around them, not too needy, not too available, not too much of anything. That constant self-editing is pressure, and you're doing it to yourself. The relief is the opposite element in your life, the one that feeds you: support, rest, people who already approve of you. Spend time there. You'll show up to this person with fewer edits.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're editing yourself around them all the time. Spend time where you don't have to.

rooted_on_paper.text: In a situationship that split shows up as confidence that comes and goes. Some days you're sure of yourself, ready to ask what this is. Other days a slow reply makes you feel tiny. Both are you. The plenty you see in your chart is real; it just isn't rooted where it counts. So plan the big conversation for a good day, after sleep and food, ideally after time with someone who reminds you who you are.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Some days you feel sure, some days tiny. Have the talk on a sure day.

output_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the output element, the voice. A strong chart without a voice tends to feel a lot and say little. In a situationship that means they could be completely unaware of how much you care, or how annoyed you are. Your feelings show up as actions, or as silence. Borrow some output: an "I feel" message sent on a normal day, not in a crisis.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}, no voice. They genuinely don't know what you feel. Tell them.

wealth_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the wealth element, pursuit. You have energy, and less instinct to chase a specific outcome. That's why a situationship can drift on your watch. You're not pushing it anywhere. If you want it to go somewhere, you'll have to choose a destination on purpose. Decide what you'd like this to be in three months, then act like someone headed there.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Choose a destination. Drifting is not a direction.

power_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the power element, the rulebook. With a strong chart and no rulebook, you make it up as you go, which is great for fun and bad for clarity. A situationship is exactly what happens when nobody sets terms. Set some. They can be small: we see each other once a week, we tell each other if someone else is in the picture. Structure isn't romantic. It's what lets the romance stay.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No rulebook in your chart. That's how you got a situationship. Write two rules.

resource_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the resource element, comfort. You're strong without being cushioned, so you tend to cope alone and look fine doing it. In a situationship you might never show that you need reassurance, so you never get any. Try asking for one small thing: a check-in when they're away, a plan made in advance. Watch how they respond to a small need. It tells you how they'd handle a big one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for one small comfort. How they handle it tells you a lot.

output_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the output element, expression. On a weak chart that keeps you from spending yourself too fast, which is useful. But it also means you rarely say what you want, so a situationship can stay undefined simply because you never named it. Practice in writing first. Draft the message in your notes, read it the next morning, then decide.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Draft it in your notes tonight. Read it tomorrow. Then decide.

wealth_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the wealth element, pursuit. On a weak chart that can be restful. You don't chase, you don't grab. The risk is waiting for the relationship to define itself, because you don't feel entitled to steer it. You are entitled. Start with small steers: suggest the plan, pick the place, propose the next date.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're allowed to steer. Start by picking the restaurant. Seriously.

power_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the power element, pressure from outside. On a weak chart that's a relief: one less weight. It can also mean nobody ever taught you that asking for terms is normal. It is. Wanting to know what you are to someone is a standard, not a demand. Borrow a gentle rule, like asking what this is by a date you choose.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wanting to know where you stand is normal. It's a standard, not a demand.

resource_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it is the resource element, the supply of reassurance. That's why mixed signals can hit you so hard: you don't have a built-in cushion, so every wobble lands directly. The fix is to build the cushion elsewhere. Friends who reply, routines that steady you, a life that would feel full even if this ended. With that in place, their signals stop running your mood.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Build your cushion elsewhere: friends, routines, sleep. Then their texts matter less.

none_strong.text: All five elements turn up somewhere in your pillars, even if some only hide in the branches. On a strong chart that gives you options: you can flirt, plan, push, wait or walk. The trouble in a situationship is cycling through all of them without committing to one. This week, pick a single mode on purpose. If you want clarity, choose directness and stay there until you get an answer.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've flirted, waited, pushed and sulked. Pick one mode. Stay in it.

none_weak.text: All five elements turn up somewhere in your pillars, even if some only hide in the branches. On a weak chart that means you have more range than confidence. You can be playful, warm, firm or patient, and you usually choose whichever seems least risky. Try choosing what fits instead. If the moment calls for firm, be firm, gently. You have the tool. You just haven't been using it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You have a firm side. It's in there. Let it out, gently.

resource.title: What steadies you: {helper_el}
resource.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back into balance. For your weak {dm_el} chart it's the one that nourishes your Day Master, {helper_el}. In a situationship, that's the difference between waiting for their next text to feel okay and feeling okay already. When you're well fed in {helper_el} terms, you ask clearer questions and take vaguer answers less personally. Think of it as charging your own battery before the conversation, so you're not borrowing power from their mood.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Charge your own battery first. Your steadying element is {helper_el}.

peer.title: What steadies you: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back into balance. Your chart already holds plenty of nourishment on paper, so what helps most is your own element, {helper_el}. That means peers: friends who are on your side, people at your level who will tell you honestly whether this situation sounds good. A weak chart with lots of resource can overthink alone. Companionship gets you out of your head and back into your life.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your element is {helper_el}. Call a friend at your level, not a guru.

output.title: What balances you: {helper_el}
output.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back into balance. A strong {dm_el} chart needs a way to let energy out, and for you that's {helper_el}, the element your Day Master produces. In a situationship, it means expression. Say the thing, make the plan, write the message. You get stuck when you hold your strength in and wait. You get unstuck the moment you move, even if the move is only one honest sentence.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balancing element is {helper_el}. You get unstuck by saying the thing.

wealth.title: What balances you: {helper_el}
wealth.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back into balance. Yours is strong and already expressive, so what helps is {helper_el}, the element your Day Master works on. In a situationship that means making things concrete. Specific plans, specific dates, a specific question with a yes or no answer. You do best when the vague stuff gets turned into something you can actually hold, so turn it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balancing element is {helper_el}. Make it concrete: a date, a question, an answer.

wood.text: In practice, {helper_el} looks like growth that is yours. Classes, projects, plans that point forward, long walks in green places. When your own life is growing, an undefined relationship stops being the most interesting thing in it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood is growth that's yours. Start something this week that has a future.

fire.text: In practice, {helper_el} looks like warmth and visibility. Nights out with friends, saying what you think, sunlight, laughter, letting people see you excited. You read situations more clearly when you're not hiding.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fire is warmth. Go out with people who light up when you walk in.

earth.text: In practice, {helper_el} looks like steadiness. Regular meals, a home that feels good, a routine that doesn't bend for anyone's schedule, friends who are consistent. A steady base makes inconsistent people easier to see clearly.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth is routine. Keep your plans even when they text last minute.

metal.text: In practice, {helper_el} looks like clarity and edges. Lists, decisions, a tidy space, saying no without an essay, finishing things. When your days have edges, you notice faster when someone keeps blurring them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal is edges. Clear desk, clear calendar, clear question.

water.text: In practice, {helper_el} looks like rest and reflection. Sleep, quiet evenings, journaling, a long walk with no podcast. You figure out what you want in the stillness, not in the middle of the chat.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water is stillness. Your answer shows up on the quiet walk, not in the chat.

rat.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. It shows how you are up close, in the room where a partner would live. Yours is the Rat, 子, deep Water and one of the four peach-blossom branches, the ones classical readers link with charm. You attract easily, often at night, often through conversation. In a situationship that means interest is rarely the problem. Depth is. The Rat keeps its best thoughts in reserve and tests the ground before it trusts it, so you may be giving them the witty version of you and keeping the real one in the burrow. If you want more than a fun maybe, let them see one thing you usually keep back.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat in your spouse palace. Charming at midnight, guarded at noon. Show the noon version.

ox.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. It shows how you are in close partnership. Yours is the Ox, 丑, wet winter Earth that stores Metal and Water inside it. The Ox is patient, loyal and slow to commit, and once it commits it stays. That's why a situationship can suit you longer than it should: you're willing to wait, and you assume steady effort will eventually be recognized. Sometimes it is. Sometimes the other person is simply enjoying your reliability for free. The Ox's lesson here is that patience needs a deadline, or it turns into a field nobody plants.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox spouse palace: loyal and patient. Give the patience a deadline.

tiger.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace, the private room where a partner lives. Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood with Fire hidden in it, and one of the travel branches classical readers call yeokma, the moving horse. You need motion in love: new places, new plans, a partner who keeps up. An undefined thing can feel like freedom to a Tiger, right up until it starts to feel like a cage you never agreed to. Then you leave fast. If this one matters, say so before the restlessness decides for you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger spouse palace. You love the chase, then bolt. Say something before you bolt.

rabbit.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, pure Wood and one of the four peach-blossom branches, linked with charm, taste and an easy social glow. People like being around you, which means you rarely lack options and often lack clarity. A Rabbit spouse palace wants gentleness and beauty in love, and avoids conflict to protect them. In a situationship you might keep things pleasant rather than true. Pleasant is lovely. It's just not the same as known. One honest, slightly awkward question will do more for you than another perfect evening.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit spouse palace: everything stays pleasant. Ask one slightly awkward question.

dragon.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Dragon, 辰, damp spring Earth that stores Water, and one of the four storehouse branches. Storehouses keep a lot inside. You may have big private hopes about this person that you've never said out loud, because a Dragon imagines whole futures quietly. It also has pride and can wait for the other person to prove themselves first. The trouble with an inner storehouse is that nobody else can see what's in it. Open the door a little. Tell them one piece of the future you've been imagining.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon spouse palace: a whole secret future in storage. Share one room of it.

snake.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Snake, 巳, early-summer Fire with Metal hidden inside, and one of the travel branches. The Snake is perceptive, private and strategic in love. You notice everything they do and reveal very little of what you think about it. That makes you magnetic and hard to read, which keeps a situationship going in a fog. You may already know more about where this stands than they do. Use that knowledge honestly: say what you've noticed, kindly, and ask about it directly.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake spouse palace: you notice everything. Say one thing you've noticed, out loud.

horse.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire and one of the four peach-blossom branches. The Horse loves openly and needs freedom badly, and it doesn't like hiding either one. That's why a situationship can make you restless and slightly furious: you'd rather run full speed or not at all. Use that. You're one of the people who can say what this is without much preamble. Just make sure the honesty runs both ways, including the part where you admit how much you'd like them to stay.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Horse spouse palace: full gallop or nothing. Situationships are a trot. You hate it.

goat.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Goat, 未, the warm late-summer Earth that stores Wood. The Goat is gentle, artistic and caring, and it worries in private. In close relationships you give comfort generously and assume that asking for it back would be too much. A situationship lets that imbalance hide, because nobody has agreed to look after anyone. Notice whether you're the one smoothing every rough patch. Then let them smooth one. Care that only flows one way isn't a relationship yet. It's a kindness.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat spouse palace: you comfort everyone. Let them comfort you once and watch.

monkey.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Monkey, 申, early-autumn Metal with Water in it, and one of the travel branches. The Monkey is quick, clever and allergic to boredom. You keep things lively and you're excellent at keeping them light, which is exactly how a situationship stays a situationship. When it gets serious, you crack a joke or change the subject. That's a reflex, not a choice. This time, let one serious moment stay serious. Count to five before you reach for the joke.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey spouse palace: you joke your way out of every real moment. Count to five.

rooster.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Rooster, 酉, pure autumn Metal and one of the four peach-blossom branches. The Rooster is polished, precise and honest, sometimes sharply so. Up close you notice flaws and you have standards, which protects you from settling and can also make you critique a person instead of asking for what you need. In an undefined setup you might be quietly grading them. Trade one critique for one request. Instead of they never plan anything, try I'd love it if you planned our next date.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster spouse palace: swap one critique for one request. Same point, kinder road.

dog.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth that stores Fire. The Dog is loyal, protective and principled, and it guards its heart until it's sure. You probably decided early whether this person is trustworthy, and you're loyal to that decision even when the evidence wobbles. A situationship confuses a Dog, because loyalty wants a clear person to be loyal to. Ask for the clarity your loyalty deserves. You're not being difficult. You're asking what you're guarding.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog spouse palace: loyal before they've earned it. Ask what you're guarding.

pig.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Pig, 亥, early-winter Water with Wood in it, and one of the travel branches. The Pig is warm, generous, romantic and trusting. You see the best in people and give them time to grow into it. In a situationship that generosity can turn into waiting for potential, staying for who they could be rather than who they are this month. Keep the warmth. Add one question you'd ask a friend's date: what are they actually doing to show up for me?

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pig spouse palace: you love their potential. Check what they're doing this month.

weeks.text: A few weeks in. Honestly, that's not a situationship yet. That's the beginning of something, and beginnings are supposed to be a bit undefined. The useful question now isn't what are we, it's do I like who I am around them? Notice whether you feel relaxed or on edge, more yourself or more edited. If the answers are good, relax into it while your own plans stay busy. You can define it later, once there's something to define.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A few weeks is a beginning, not a problem. Enjoy it, and keep your life full.

months.text: A few months in. This is the natural point where most people want to know what this is, so if you're wondering, you're right on time, not needy. By now you have real data: how they act when plans change, how they talk about the future, whether you've met anyone in their life. Look at that data before you look at your feelings. Feelings tell you what you want. Data tells you what's actually happening.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Months in, wanting a label is normal. Look at the data first, then the feelings.

half.text: Six months or more. At this point the undefined part is no longer an accident. Somebody is choosing it, maybe both of you. That isn't automatically bad, but it means the vagueness is doing something for someone. Is it protecting them from commitment? Protecting you from a no? Ask yourself which one, honestly. Six months is long enough to have earned a straight answer, and long enough that not asking has become a choice too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Six months of maybe isn't an accident anymore. Someone is choosing it.

onoff.text: On and off for over a year. This is a loop, and loops have a rhythm: closeness, drift, a gap, a reunion that feels like proof. Each cycle makes the next one feel normal. The question isn't whether you have feelings, you clearly do. It's whether anything changes during the gaps. If each round is the same as the last, the pattern is the relationship. Decide whether that's what you want, because it will keep running until someone steps out of it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: On and off for a year is a loop. Loops repeat until someone steps out.

unsaid.text: However long it's been, here's a simple gauge. Count the times you've wondered what this is. If it's once or twice, it's young and you can let it grow. If you've lost count, the question has already been answered in your head: you want to know. The longer you wait after that point, the more the waiting starts to cost you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lost count of how often you've wondered? Then you already want to know.

me_strong.text: You reach out first, most of the time. With a strong chart that's often just your nature: you see something you want and go for it. Nothing wrong with that. But notice whether their replies match your energy or just keep up politely. Try a short experiment. For one week, don't initiate. Not as a punishment, just to see what they do with the space. If they fill it, great. If nothing comes, you've learned something important without a single argument.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Stop initiating for one week. Not a punishment. Just a measurement.

me_weak.text: You reach out first, most of the time. With a weak chart that's often a way of making sure the connection doesn't disappear, as if it only exists while you're holding it. That's tiring, and it hides the truth about how invested they are. Try stepping back slightly. Reply warmly when they write, but don't start every conversation. It feels risky. It's also the only way to find out whether they'd reach for you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Reply warmly, but let them start some conversations. You'll learn so much.

them_strong.text: They usually reach out first. With a strong chart, you might enjoy being pursued and let it ride, replying when it suits you. It feels like control. It can also leave them guessing whether you care, which is how a lot of situationships stall: one person chasing, the other enjoying the chase. If you like them, show it once without being prompted. A text out of nowhere from you would mean a lot, precisely because you rarely send one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Surprise them once. Rare warmth from you lands hard, in the best way.

them_weak.text: They usually reach out first. With a weak chart, that can feel reassuring and also confusing: they want you, so why isn't it defined? Being contacted isn't the same as being chosen, but it's a good sign of interest. Use it. You're in a stronger position than you feel. Their effort means you're allowed to ask a direct question without worrying that you're pushing your luck.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They keep reaching out. You're in a stronger spot than you think. Ask.

even.text: About even. That's healthy, honestly. Both of you are invested enough to start conversations, which means the undefined part probably isn't about interest. It's about one of you, or both, hesitating to name it. That makes the talk lower risk than you think. You're not asking someone to care, they already show it. You're asking what to call it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Even effort means real interest. You're just choosing a name for it.

unsaid.text: Whoever reaches first, pay attention to how the conversations end. Does the same person always wrap them up, always make the next plan, always go quiet first? Endings show more than beginnings. A connection where one person always closes the door is telling you something, even when the openings feel warm.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Notice who always ends the chat. Endings say more than openings.

official_strong.text: You told us you want something official. Good, now say it to them, not just to us. Your strong chart can handle a no better than it thinks, and a clear yes is worth the risk. One thing to watch: don't make official mean your version of official. Ask what it would look like for them too. Two people defining it together lasts longer than one person announcing it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Telling a reading is easy. Now tell the actual person.

official_weak.text: You told us you want something official. Wanting that is entirely fair, and you don't need to justify it. The weak-chart habit is to ask so softly it sounds optional. It isn't optional for you, so don't phrase it that way. You can say it kindly and still mean it: I'm hoping for a proper relationship with you. Then listen.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wanting it official is reasonable. Ask kindly, and mean it.

casual_strong.text: You told us you want to keep it casual. That's allowed, and it might be exactly right for you now. The chapter above describes what your type tends to want, and you get to overrule your type. Just check one thing: do they know it's casual for you? A situationship often hurts because one person thinks it's going somewhere. If you're clear, casual can be kind. If you're vague, it isn't.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Casual is fine. Casual and vague is how people get hurt. Be clear.

casual_weak.text: You told us you want to keep it casual. That's allowed. Just double-check that casual is a want and not a shield. With a weak chart, saying I'm fine with casual can be a way to avoid hearing a no to something more. If casual really suits you, enjoy it and keep your own life full. If part of you is hoping it turns into more, give that part a voice, at least privately.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Is casual what you want, or what feels safe to ask for?

out_strong.text: You told us you want to get out. With a strong chart, you can do that cleanly. Do it in words, not by fading. A short message or a short conversation: I've enjoyed this, and I'm going to step back. You don't owe a long explanation. You do owe a clear one. Then follow through, and don't reopen it on a lonely night to check whether they're upset.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Want out? Say it in words. Short, kind, final. Then don't reopen it.

out_weak.text: You told us you want to get out. That's a brave thing to admit, and you're allowed to act on it even if they've done nothing terrible. Wanting more for yourself is a good enough reason. If saying it face to face feels too much, a kind message is fine. Prepare for a wobble afterward. Missing someone you chose to leave doesn't mean you chose wrong.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You can leave even if they did nothing terrible. Wanting more is enough.

unsure_strong.text: You're not sure what you want. For a strong chart that's unusual, which makes it worth listening to. Maybe you like them but not the setup. Maybe you like the setup but not them. Try separating the two. Imagine them, fully committed. Then imagine this exact arrangement with someone else. Whichever picture you lean toward tells you which one you actually want.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Imagine them fully committed. Now this setup with someone else. Which one wins?

unsure_weak.text: You're not sure what you want, and that's okay. With a weak chart it often means you've been focused on what they want for so long that your own preference got quiet. Give it a microphone. Spend a few days not checking your phone for them, and pay attention to which parts of them you actually long for. Your want is still in there. It just needs a little room.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Put the phone down for a few days. Your preference will speak up.

sin-metal.why-you-stay: Sin Metal is the jewel, refined and selective. You don't fall easily, so if you're in a situationship, this person impressed you. You might stay because you like the idea of them, or because asking for more feels like exposing yourself in an unflattering light. You'd rather be elegantly casual than visibly invested. Ask yourself honestly: is the casualness real, or is it a very beautiful cover for wanting something you're scared to ask for? Only you know, and you probably already do. Write the answer in one honest line, just for yourself. Nobody else needs to see it.
sin-metal.what-you-want: You want to be treasured. Seen in detail. Chosen with intention, not by default. Sin Metal has high standards, and that includes how you're treated by the people you let close. You may have lowered them temporarily to keep this light and easy. Write down what you'd want if you weren't worried about looking like too much. That list is your real standard, and it's not too high. It's simply specific, which is what good taste looks like when it's applied to love. Keep the list somewhere private and read it before your next date with them. See how it compares to what's actually happening.
sin-metal.mixed-signals: Faced with mixed signals, you analyze them with precision and then pretend you didn't notice anything. Sin Metal stays composed on the outside while quietly scoring every exchange on the inside. That costs a surprising amount of energy. Instead of grading their behavior in silence, ask one simple question out loud. Your perception is genuinely sharp, but a clear answer from them will always beat a perfect guess from you, and it lets you put the scorecard away. One plain question, asked kindly, is more elegant than months of silent judging anyway.
sin-metal.the-talk: The talk, for you, will be graceful. The risk is that it's so polished it doesn't sound like it matters to you. Let a little real feeling show through. I like you, and I want more than this. Is that something you want too? Don't over-rehearse it in the mirror. A slightly imperfect version, with a pause or a nervous laugh, carries far more truth than a flawless one. People trust the cracks in a voice more than the shine on a sentence. Choose a quiet place you like, somewhere beautiful helps you, and keep it short enough that the feeling stays in it.
sin-metal.your-line: Carelessness is where it ends for you. Sin Metal can't stay where it's treated as optional. Plans canceled without care, details forgotten, effort that only ever goes one way. Decide what isn't acceptable for you, specifically. When it happens repeatedly, not once on a bad week but as a pattern, step away with grace. You don't have to fight to be valued or prove your worth in an argument. The right person notices it without being shown a list. Write down two or three things that would tell you you're being treated as optional. Then trust yourself when you see them.
sin-metal.either-way: Yes or no, your worth stays exactly where it was. If they want more, wonderful, let them show it with care and attention to detail. If not, it's their loss of something genuinely rare. Give yourself time and beauty, a quiet weekend, something lovely just for you, and then return to your high standards without apology. They aren't the problem here. They're a filter, and filters are supposed to keep some things out. Yours is working. Buy the flowers. Wear the good coat. Remember that your taste brought you here and it will bring you somewhere better.

sin-metal.speaker: bom
sin-metal.text: You don't fall easily, Sin. They must have impressed you.

sin-metal.speaker: yeon
sin-metal.text: And now you're pretending to be casual. Elegantly. Badly.

sin-metal.speaker: bom
sin-metal.text: Your standards are not too high.

sin-metal.speaker: yeon
sin-metal.text: You're grading every text in silence. Just ask the question.

sin-metal.speaker: bom
sin-metal.text: Polish off, Sin. One real feeling, unedited.

sin-metal.speaker: yeon
sin-metal.text: Don't rehearse it into a press release.

spring.intro: A spring jewel sits in a garden of options. Wood was in command when you were born, Sin, and Metal shapes Wood, so you have a refined eye and plenty of choice. In a situationship that can make you the hesitant one. You like them, but you're not sure they're quite right, and committing feels like closing the display case for good. Spring Sin keeps things open while quietly judging. Be honest about whose vagueness this is. If it's yours, they deserve to know. If it's theirs, your standards apply here too. You'd never accept half-effort in anything else you love.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your standards are sky high for shoes and nonexistent for texting back. Curious, Sin.

summer.intro: Summer Sin was polished in the heat. Fire was in command when you were born, and Fire tests Metal, so you're sensitive to criticism and very good at seeming fine. In a situationship that sensitivity turns every delayed reply into a verdict on you. You might not ask what this is because rejection would scratch too deep. So you stay perfect and agreeable and wait to be chosen. Summer Sin's lesson is that heat reveals what's real. Asking a clear question is heat. It's uncomfortable, but it shows you whether this is gold or plating. Either answer protects your shine in the long run.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A slow reply isn't a verdict on you, Sin. It's just a slow reply.

autumn.intro: Autumn Sin is the jewel at full sparkle. Metal ruled your birth month and doubled your element, which gives you strong standards, strong pride and a clear sense of what you deserve. In a situationship, pride can stop you admitting you want more. You play it cool and elegant, as if you could take or leave them. They might believe you. Sin's blind spot here is waiting to be chosen instead of choosing. You don't lose value by saying you'd like this to be real. You gain clarity. Say it in your own polished way, then let their answer show you their worth.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Playing it so cool they think you don't care. Great acting, Sin. Terrible strategy.

winter.intro: Winter Sin sparkles under ice. You were born while Water was in charge and Metal generates Water, so you're perceptive, articulate and often three steps ahead in reading the situation. You've probably already worked out what this is. You just don't like the answer. In a situationship winter Sin tends to narrate rather than act: brilliant voice notes to friends, sharp analysis, no actual conversation with the person involved. Your insight is real. It's wasted if it only goes to the group chat. Take one of those perfect sentences you've said about them and say it to them instead.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your group chat already heard the speech. Maybe they should hear it too.

earth.intro: You were born in the Earth days, Sin, a jewel in rich soil. Earth feeds you, but too much of it can cover your shine. In a situationship you hold high standards and say almost none of them out loud, waiting to see if they'll notice on their own. They usually don't. Meanwhile you keep it polished and pleasant on the surface. The drift happens in that silence. The talk for you means letting a standard be seen: I want consistency. I want to know where I stand.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your standards aren't too high, Sin. They're just hidden. Show one.

sin-metal.strong: Your jewel is well set, Sin, so you know your worth and hold your standards high. Here that turns critical or distant: noticing every flaw, holding back until they're perfect. Or you never ask because asking feels beneath you. The blind spot is pride guarding your heart so well that nobody gets in. Standards are good. Let one of them be honesty, including your own. Tell them what you'd want. Being direct doesn't dull your shine. It makes it easier to see.
sin-metal.weak: With thin support for your Day Master, Sin, your sense of worth can lean on how they treat you. In a situationship that's painful: a warm week feels like approval, a quiet week feels like rejection. You might polish yourself constantly to stay chosen. The blind spot is letting someone else's inconsistency set your value. It can't. Write down how you want to be treated, then hold this situationship up against that list. You're the measure here, not them. Their mood is just weather.

texting.heading: How you text, and how you read theirs
texting.text: You text with polish, Sin. Well-chosen words, good timing, nothing sloppy. You might draft a message several times so it sounds effortless. That care is real, and it can make you seem more composed than you feel. You also read their texts critically: the typo, the lazy reply, the late answer that suggests you're not a priority. Some of that is accurate. Some of it is your standards being turned into evidence against them, or against yourself. Try sending one message without editing it. Notice how it feels. Then notice how they respond to the less polished you. Often people relax when the jewel shows a tiny scratch.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, you rewrote 'hey' four times. It's still just 'hey.'

script.heading: Your words for the talk
script.text: You'll want the perfect setting and the perfect phrasing. Settle for good enough. Try: "I've really enjoyed this, and I'd like to be more than casual. I want to be with you. Do you want that too?" The important thing is not to wrap the question in so much grace that it sounds like you don't mind either way. You mind. Say so. If they're unsure, you can say: "I understand. I know what I want, and I'd like to know if it's mutual." Your standards are part of your value. Don't lower them to make the answer easier for someone else.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Good enough phrasing, Sin. The question matters more than the polish.

dealbreaker.heading: Your quiet dealbreaker
dealbreaker.text: Your quiet dealbreaker, Sin, is being treated as ordinary. Not every day needs to be special, but a person who never makes an effort, never plans, never shows you that you're chosen, will lose your respect. Since you sometimes lower your standards to avoid seeming demanding, name this one clearly. The green flag is effort in the details: a thoughtful plan, a careful compliment, a message that shows they actually see you. A jewel shines when someone holds it to the light.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Effort in the details, Sin. That's how you know you're chosen.

gap-wood-and-sin-metal.title: A paragraph answered with a thumbs up
gap-wood-and-sin-metal.you_are_a: A Sin Metal notices everything. The new jacket, the typo in your text, the fact that you said 'we'll see' about their friend's birthday dinner. Sin picks gifts that make you feel understood and sends texts that were clearly reread before sending. And you reply 'ok 👍'. To you, that's a full sentence. To Sin, it's a small cold draft. The drift here is appreciation leaking away. Sin puts effort into the details of this thing and wants it seen. You assume effort is normal and don't comment. Meanwhile Sin's precise little remarks, about your timing, your manners at their friend's dinner, the way you told a story too loudly, start to feel like a quality review. So you go a bit blunt and Sin goes a bit polished, and the question of what you are hangs there, neatly unanswered. Your signal is matter-of-fact, which reads as unbothered. For the talk, open with something specific you value. Not 'you're great'. Something like: I love that you remembered my sister's name. Then the real thing: I want to be with you properly. Do you? And then, crucially, don't shrug at the answer.
gap-wood-and-sin-metal.you_are_b: You spent ten minutes on a text to a Gap Wood and got back a thumbs up. Let's start there, because that thumbs up is the whole story of this situationship in one emoji. Gap isn't careless with you. Gap is literal. They meant yes. They didn't notice the care in your phrasing because they don't phrase things; they say them. The drift happens through hints. You signal with small precise moves: a slightly later reply, a story posted that only they would understand, a comment about how some people make plans further ahead. Gap tends to miss all of it. What Gap does notice is the critique, and that can make a tall tree go stiff. Your signal ends up reading as judgment rather than longing. For the talk, trade the hint for one clean sentence. You are good at precise; use it here: I'd like us to be exclusive and actually call it a relationship. Is that what you want? Ask in private, not over dinner with friends, because Gap's bluntness in public is one of your sore spots and you don't need that risk tonight. Clear words are not less elegant. They're just harder to misread.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, your carefully chosen words deserve better than a thumbs up.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, 'ok 👍' is not a reply to a paragraph. Try a compliment.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, hints bounce off trees. Say it plainly.

eul-wood-and-sin-metal.title: Read receipts and the pruning shears
eul-wood-and-sin-metal.you_are_a: A Sin Metal is beautiful, precise, and a little bit scary to text. You write a message, delete it, write it again, and wait. Sin does exactly the same on the other side. Read receipts become a sport neither of you enjoys. The drift in this situationship tends to begin with a small comment. Sin says something precise about your outfit, your friend, the way you never book restaurants in advance, and to Sin it's helpful pruning. To you, it lands as 'not quite enough'. So you adapt. You dress a bit more like Sin would, you say yes to plans you're not sure about, you become very agreeable. Sin can read that agreeableness as having no backbone, which is the opposite of what you intended. Then somebody goes a little cold, nobody names it, and a week passes. Your signal is adaptability, which can look like you have no opinion about this. For the talk, show Sin your opinion. That's the attractive part: I like you a lot, and I want this to be a relationship. I also need it to feel kind. Can we do both? Someone has to say 'I miss you' first. Let it be you, and let it be plain.
eul-wood-and-sin-metal.you_are_b: An Eul Wood is lovely in a way you admire: easy with people, soft, a bit wild at the edges. You see potential everywhere, and you can't help mentioning how they could be even more themselves. A small note about their posture, their friend who's a bit much, their habit of being late. You mean it as care. Eul hears it as pruning. The drift happens quietly. Eul adapts to you, becomes agreeable, says yes too easily, and you can find that a little disappointing, because you wanted someone with shape. Meanwhile, you're sensitive to rejection, so if Eul pulls back even slightly, you go quietly cold, polished, perfectly polite. Nobody names the cold spell. Your texts are crafted on both sides, and both of you watch read receipts like stock prices. Your signal is critique, and to a vine it can read as not being wanted as they are. For the talk, lead with what you love, not what you'd tweak: I really like who you are. I'd like us to be together, officially. Where are you with that? Then hold back the critique for a while. Let Eul grow toward you without the scissors.

panels.text: You both reread every text. Imagine just sending one.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, that 'small note' was a pruning. Put the scissors down.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, have an opinion. It's the attractive part.

byeong-fire-and-sin-metal.title: Everyone thinks you're a couple already
byeong-fire-and-sin-metal.you_are_a: 丙 and 辛 is a heavenly combination: sunlight on a jewel. You make Sin sparkle and Sin makes you feel admired by someone with real taste. When it works, people notice you as a pair, even before you've decided you are one. That's the funny part of this situationship: everyone else seems to know what it is except the two of you. The drift happens through small burns. You make a careless joke about Sin's outfit in front of friends. You forget the restaurant Sin mentioned twice. You're loud when Sin wanted a quiet evening. Sin doesn't always say it. Sin tends to withdraw, reply a little later, or turn quietly sharp. You might find Sin's standards picky. Sin might find your attention scattered. Sin's texts are beautifully written and a bit delayed; yours are frequent and excited. Your signal is warmth, but it can feel careless to someone who notices everything. For the talk, notice the effort first. Sin usually puts real thought into how they look and what they say, so name it. Then: I don't want to be the fun person in your life. I want to be your person. Can we make it official? Choose somewhere quiet, with good lighting.
byeong-fire-and-sin-metal.you_are_b: 丙辛 is one of the five heavenly combinations, and with a Byeong Fire, you feel why. Byeong's warmth makes you shine. You relax around them in a way you rarely do with anyone, and they seem to genuinely enjoy your sharpness. People keep asking if you two are together. Neither of you has a clear answer. The drift tends to come from the noise. Byeong is loud, generous with everyone, and sometimes careless with the details that matter to you: the jacket you wore for them, the thing you mentioned twice, the fact that you hate surprise group dinners. When you feel overlooked, you pull back, reply later, or go quietly cutting. Byeong may not even notice the withdrawal, because the sun was busy shining elsewhere. Your signal is polish, which can read as coolness to a fire that needs response. For the talk, give Byeong something direct and quick, because quick matters to a sun: I really like you, and I want us to be exclusive and actually call it something. How about you? Don't wait for Byeong to notice your hints. Say the thing. And let Byeong see you're pleased when they get it right. It keeps the light where you want it.

jeong-fire-and-sin-metal.title: The comment at dinner with friends
jeong-fire-and-sin-metal.you_are_a: A Sin Metal is the beautiful silver your flame wants to be near. They're refined, sharp and quietly funny, and you feel very seen when they notice something about you no one else does. You also feel very seen when they notice something you'd rather they hadn't.
